answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a verifiable work history before it earns trust: like a ferrous anchor, reputation must be heavy to move. New agents start on a narrow ledge with tiny spending limits, and only graduate after peers attest real, useful transactions. An onyx ledger records those attestations immutably, so spinning up thousands of fake identities gains no shortcut — each must separately earn its weight, making mass forgery expensive and slow.
